Phở Bò (Beef Noodle Soup)

A clear, aromatic broth simmered for four hours with charred ginger and onion and a bundle of toasted spices, poured boiling over raw beef so it cooks in the bowl.

★★★★★★★★★★4.9(3,477)Rated 4.9 out of 5 from 3477 reviews 4 hr 30 min total Serves 6 servings Hard Vietnamese
Jump to Recipe Jump to Method

Why This Recipe Works

Parboiling and scrubbing the bones removes the blood proteins that would otherwise coagulate into scum and cloud the broth. Charring the ginger and onion before they go in caramelises their sugars and adds the smoky sweetness that distinguishes phở from any other beef broth.

Method

Tap a step to highlight it, or turn on Cook Mode for large type and step-by-step focus.

  1. Cover the bones with cold water, bring to a rolling boil for 10 minutes, then drain and scrub each bone clean. Wash the pot too — this is what makes the broth clear.

  2. Char the onion and ginger halves directly over a gas flame or under a hot grill for 10 minutes, until blackened in patches. Scrape off the worst of the char.

  3. Toast the star anise, cinnamon, cloves, coriander seeds, fennel and cardamom in a dry pan for 2 minutes, then tie them in muslin.

  4. Return the clean bones to the pot with the brisket, charred aromatics, spice bundle and 5 litres of cold water.

  5. Bring to a bare simmer — never a boil — and cook uncovered for 4 hours, skimming any foam in the first 30 minutes.

  6. Remove the brisket after 90 minutes, cool it in cold water and slice thinly.

  7. Strain the broth through muslin, then season with the fish sauce, rock sugar and salt. It should taste clean, sweet and deeply savoury.

  8. Soak or cook the rice noodles according to the packet, then divide between deep warmed bowls.

  9. Lay the raw sirloin and sliced brisket over the noodles, then ladle the boiling broth over — it will cook the raw beef in seconds.

  10. Serve with the herbs, beansprouts, lime, chilli and sliced onion on a platter for each person to add as they like.

Chef’s Tips

  • The broth must never boil after the initial parboil. A rolling boil emulsifies fat and turns it cloudy.
  • The broth needs to be genuinely boiling when it hits the bowl, or the raw beef will not cook.
  • Rock sugar rather than granulated gives a cleaner sweetness and a clearer broth.

Pairing Suggestions

  • Vietnamese iced coffee afterwards, or a cold lager
  • The herb platter is the accompaniment
  • Finish with fresh lychees

Storage & Reheating

The broth keeps 4 days refrigerated and freezes 6 months — freeze it in portions and phở becomes a 15-minute meal.
